why: The minimum cost to reach a target with a jump window: dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i-k..i-1]) with dp[0] = 0, and the window minimum is kept in a monotonic deque so the DP is O(n), not O(nk).
hints: The cheapest way to stop at point i comes from the cheapest of the k points before it. Write that recurrence first.
dp[0] = 0 (start at x = 0); dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[j]) for i-k <= j < i. The answer is dp[n]. Directly this is O(nk), too slow for 3*10^5.
Keep a deque of indices with increasing dp values: drop the front when it leaves the window, drop the back while its dp >= the new dp. The front is always the window minimum.
pitfalls: You must stop at point n and pay its cost.
